# Operations Academia — Build Spec for the v2 Rewrite

**Goal.** Replace the Awesome Tables (paid) + Google Forms + Google Sheets stack with the site's own submission form writing to Firestore, a scheduled GitHub Action committing static JSON into this repository, and a static filterable card list — the architecture of `stouras.com/lit/`. Add Firebase sign-in, e-mail alerts (new jobs, new candidates, job-market news, website updates) and the `/lit/` feedback → resolution loop.

**Provenance of this document.** Sections A (sheet schemas), C, E and most of F/H are merged from seven parallel readers of the two repositories. Everything marked **[verified in repo]** was additionally checked directly in `/home/user/OperationsAcademia.github.io` on 2026‑08‑15 and was *not* covered by the readers — a partial `v2/` prototype already exists and must be reconciled with this spec rather than rebuilt. Uncertainties are collected in **Open questions** at the end.

Machine-readable dump of every sheet/tab/column (headers, roles, distinct-value vocabularies, formula derivations): `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user/a668473d-68da-5bf0-90c1-856dfa2dbbb0/scratchpad/oa-sheets-schema.json` (340 KB).

## A. Current state

### A.1 Site chrome (`operationsacademia.org`)

Hand-maintained static site on the Pixelarity "Iconic" template, served by GitHub Pages from the repo root, `CNAME = www.operationsacademia.org`, no Jekyll config, no build step.

**Page skeleton** — identical on all 16 interior pages (`index.html` is the one variant, `body class="homepage"`, banner + `ul.pennants` instead of the card):

```
#page-wrapper
  #header-wrapper > .container#header      fixed white bar: a#logo + <nav id="nav"></nav>  (nav is EMPTY in HTML)
  #main-wrapper                            brand blue #3B7DBC + tiled bg.svg
    .container#page
      .title-heading > h2                  white heading on the blue
      #main                                the white rounded card (border-radius .5em, padding 4em 2.5em)
        .row > .12u#content                ALL page content, as inline-styled divs
<div data-include="/partials/footer.html"></div>
```

**Script order is load-bearing** and identical on all 17 pages:
`assets/js/ypo-parakolouthisi.js` (defines global `ga`) → `assets/js/navigationMenu.js` (assigns the whole nav tree as one `innerHTML` string to `#nav`) → `jquery.min.js` (1.11.3) → `jquery.dropotron.min.js` → `skel.min.js` (3.0.1) → `https://awesome-table.com/AwesomeTableInclude.js` → `assets/js/util.js` → `assets/js/main.js`. The footer pair (`<div data-include>` + `assets/js/include-partials.js`, a 27-line `fetch` + `outerHTML` replace that also fills `.js-current-year`) is emitted *before* that block.

- **Mobile nav depends on `main.js`.** At ≤840 px `main.css` sets `#header-wrapper{display:none}` and `#page-wrapper{padding-top:44px}` unconditionally; `#titleBar`/`#navPanel` are created at runtime by `main.js` from `$('#logo').html()` and `$('#nav').navList()` (275 px, left, swipe). Drop jQuery/skel/util/main.js and a page has **no navigation at all below 840 px**.
- **`assets/css/main.css` (2,688 lines) is the sole source of truth.** `assets/sass/` is stale template source that was never recompiled: `libs/_vars.scss` has *empty* `$palette`/`$font` maps and `main.scss` still says `body{color:#656b74}` where the shipped CSS says `#222222`. Every site-specific style (sponsor bar, `.button.blue`, link colours, logo `colorReplace` animation, footer colours) exists only in `main.css`. **Never recompile the sass.**
- **Palette** (literal hex, no CSS custom properties except `--logo-h-min/-vw/-max` on `.sponsor-logos`): brand blue `#3B7DBC` (hover `#4B8DCC`, active `#2489a8`), navy `#343e49` (hover `#444E59`, `#navPanel` `#242E39`), page bg `#f5f7fa`, body text `#222222`, headings `#313a45`, link `#0645ad` / visited `#0b0080`, footer link `#a1a6ac`, surfaces `#FFF`, sponsor bar `#f9f9f9` on `#e2e8f0`, accents `.cuhk-text #660066` / `.msom-text #f15a22`, shadow `0 0.05em 0.15em 0 rgba(0,0,0,0.15)`. The grey intro panel is **inline style**, not a class: `background:rgb(249,249,249); border:1px solid rgb(204,204,204); text-align:justify` with a floated `images/information.png`.
- **Typography**: `'Source Sans Pro'` only (`@import` at the top of main.css, 300/300i/600/900), body weight 300, line-height 1.70em, sizes in **points** — 16pt → 14pt (≤1680) → 13pt (≤1280) → 12pt (≤736), and `text-align: justify` on `body` at ≤736 px. Font Awesome 4.6.3 via a second `@import`.
- **Grid**: skel 3.0.1 compiled. `.container` 1320 → 1140 → 960 → 95% → 100%; `.row` float-based, negative-margin gutters 60 → 50 → 40 → 30 → 20 px; columns `Nu` (`.12u`, `.6u`, `.2u`), breakpoint variants written with literal parentheses (`class="6u 12u(narrower)"`).
- **Nav tree** lives only in `assets/js/navigationMenu.js` (lines 24‑46 live; 1‑23 a commented 2024‑25 copy). Four top-level items with dropdowns, **relative extensionless hrefs** (`href="jobs"`) — which is why a page one directory down needs its own absolute-href copy (`v2/assets/oa-nav.js`). Adding a page = 3 edits: `navigationMenu.js`, `sitemap.xml`, optionally `partials/footer.html`.
- **Analytics** is the legacy Universal Analytics snippet (`UA-47739718-1`), dead since July 2023, but ~40 inline `ga('send', …)` handlers depend on the global existing.
- **Awesome Tables is a leaf dependency.** `AwesomeTableInclude.js` is loaded on all 17 pages but nothing in the repo's own JS or CSS references it. Removing it blanks exactly five embeds and changes nothing else. jQuery / skel / util / main.js *are* load-bearing.

**The five live Awesome Table views:** `jobs.html` `-O_tq18fckswU28d7JCQ` · `candidates.html` `-O4FOuoyvD6mHL9CF44i` · `previous-markets.html` `-O4FTJkB-AhEOsYTAw3b` · `universities.html` `-Oc3gWtzjGy38U9Czxvv` (lowercase `data-viewid`) · `recent-faculty.html` `-OYDeV1dwRpU-q9yHb2X` (lowercase). `placements.html` has its AT div **commented out**.

### A.2 The Sheets / Awesome Tables data stack

Six spreadsheets, each with the same three-tab pattern: a **raw** tab (the Google Form response sheet), a **display** tab (row 1 = headers, **row 2 = the Awesome Table control row** carrying roles like `StringFilter`, `CategoryFilter - Hidden`, `csvFilter - Hidden`, `DateFilter - Hidden`, `CardsContent`, `MapsLat`/`MapsLong`/`MapsTooltip`, `Sidebar`), and a **card-template** tab whose A1 repeats the CardsContent column name and whose A2 holds the card HTML (mixing `{{Col}}` in the collapsed header/`ga()` call with `${"Col"}` in the expanded table) plus `<style>`/`<script>` columns.

Display rows are built by **positional formulas** reading raw row N — not a query. Verified: the 80 `jobsData` timestamps equal the first 80 raw timestamps exactly.

| Sheet | File id | Raw rows | Display rows | Date range |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Job Postings (`/jobs`) | `1YgTajXa5W1r4Ekm2zkFGQoQFNiE3C82l4_54aMYizok` | 129 | **80** (`jobsData`) | raw to 2025‑10‑21, display to 2025‑08‑13 |
| Past job postings (`/previous-markets`) | `1d0_XxHBYKFEvYDQWEJzIipFmvAo5w9t4jd1hEHTgDzs` | 51 (`rawData`) | **93** | 2014‑04‑08 … 2015‑02‑10 |
| Candidates (`/candidates`) | `1-hpvbSnA5DDY1RhdqlBRHC1wFfLMGKtw9egzBa4NZ7A` | 104 (`rawData`) | 104 | 2018‑08‑25 … 2026‑07‑29 |
| Confirmed Placements (`/placements`) | `14x2Fu_A3L_RXdMRnEbgBdSYbebaVrVdXVHMJ2EytrwQ` | 173 (`rawData`) | 173 | 2014‑12‑03 … 2025‑03‑12 |
| Recent Faculty (`/recent-faculty`) | `16j0bQulL7jWIpajmVRzlJZmz6rf8k_r7z_4enfXBAuk` | 190 + 94 helper | **212** | 2015‑01‑05 … 2025‑09‑21 |
| List of Universities (`/universities`) | `1aW8z50zk98vmsrt6llJySvPH2ID0s0GtT_4Xh-J0rMw` | — | 144 (`Universities`) | no dates |

**Job Postings — raw tab (the form), 18 columns:** Timestamp · Job Market Year · First Name · Last Name · Your email · University Name/Institution · School Name, Department/Area/Group Name · Type of Institution (`Business School`|`University`) · Job entry level (multi-select, 10 observed combinations of 5 values) · Apply by (exact date) · Apply by (comments) · (if applicable) INFORMS interview comments/deadline · Country location of the University (**un-normalised**: `UK` vs `United Kingdom`, `United States` vs `USA`, `Hong Kong SAR`, `Shenzhen, China`) · (optional) Posted online at · (optional) PDF upload (Drive URL) · Does your Institution have any of the following? (6 checkboxes, 29 combinations) · Name of Area Faculty Coordinator/Department Chair · E-mail of that chair · **(optional) Comments/Feedback**.

**Job Postings — display tab `jobsData`, 30 columns.** Cols 1‑6 are plain mirrors. Derived: col 7 `Apply by` = long-date `TEXT(raw date)` + `". "` + comments, or the literal `"Until filled."`; col 8 = INFORMS comments else `"NA"`; cols 19‑23 `HasSeminars?/HasPhD?/HasMBA?/HasExecEd?/HasUndergrad?` are an `IF(SEARCH(...))` fan-out of the checkbox answer; col 12 `Characteristics` = concatenation of 19‑23; col 16 = `"Our School/ Department have: "` & the checkbox answer; cols 10/11/26 build HTML anchors; col 24 `Date posted` and col 25 `Deadline` are **bucket formulas** whose full vocabulary is unobservable (today they evaluate only to `Older posts` and `{Expired, Until filled}`; the archive copy evaluates to `Since last June` and `{Expired, NA}` — proof they are recomputed, not stored). Cols 29‑30 are unnamed overflow holding a stray second `Featured` flag + badge.

**Stored HTML shapes** (all `target="_blank"`): ad link `<a href="https://drive.google.com/open?id=ID" target="_blank">link to Job ad</a>` (archive variant `…/file/d/ID/view?usp=sharing">PDF file</a>` or `Word file`), fallback the literal string `NA`; posted-online `<a href="URL" …>link</a>`, fallback `<a href="http://www.operationsacademia.org/" …>Operations Academia</a>`; further-info `…/universities?filterA=<University/Institution>`; featured badge `<div class="row"><div class="col-md-12"><span class="label label-primary" …>Featured</span></div></div>`.

Display adds `Name`, `Currently = Position & " (" & Affiliation & ")"`, anchor columns, a `Presents on…` csvFilter that drops `Saturday` and maps legacy session codes (`SB15, TA10, TC22` → `Sunday, Tuesday`) — **and duplicates that column twice (16 and 17)**. Display col 14 `Profile checked` is the intended approval column and is **empty in all 104 rows**.

**Confirmed Placements — raw, 13 columns:** Timestamp · First/Last Name · E-mail · Web Page · "Have you completed our survey?" · comments — plus six **curator-added** columns: Joining University/Institution, Undergraduate Institution, Note, Job Market Year, PhD Institution, Joining Position. Older rows store the rank inside the institution string (`Assistant Professor (INSEAD)`); newer rows split it out, so the display `Joining` column begins with `", "` on the 94 rows whose position is blank. Display = raw rows 1‑190 mirrored + **22 hand-appended rows** (8 lifted from a 94-person supplementary tab where 20 rows park the placement string in the *comments* column). **Universities — 144 rows, 17 columns:** University (full label) · University/Institution (**the join key**) · School · Department · School Department · Campus location link · Address · Latitude/Longitude (`MapsLat`/`MapsLong`, geocoded by hand via an add-on on a scratch tab) · Faculty-link · Faculty (anchor with inline `ga()`) · and five deep-link anchors of the shape `http://www.operationsacademia.org/<page>.html?filter<X>=<University/ Institution>`: recent-faculty `filterE` (recent hires), recent-faculty `filterF` (PhD alumni), candidates `filterE`, jobs `filterD`, previous-markets `filterD`.

### A.3 What is actually broken today (the reasons for the rewrite)

1. **The live page is 49 submissions stale.** `jobsData` stops at 2025‑08‑13 while `rawData` runs to 2025‑10‑21: rows 81‑129 have no display row and never reached the site, because the mirror formulas were never dragged past row 82.
2. **Approval is a convention, not a mechanism.** For Jobs and Candidates there is no OK column — the curator types `OK` into the last free-text *form* field (Jobs 58/129, Candidates 30/104) and it gates nothing (41 of the 80 published job rows carry no OK). Only Recent Faculty has a working `isOK`; Placements' is broken; Candidates' `Profile checked` is unused.
3. **Vendor lock and cost.** Awesome Tables is paid, the card layout lives in a spreadsheet cell, and Google Forms/Drive hold the submissions.
4. **Data quality**: junk `Job Market Year` values (`200`, `100`, `2023-24`), un-normalised countries, `12/1/12014`, duplicate columns, double-spaced names, the leading `", "` on `Joining`, dead template references (`Confirmed Placement`, `Current Faculty Position`, `Note HTML`).
5. The Past-postings archive display tab (93) has **more rows than its own raw tab** (51) — it was accumulated by hand, so raw is not the source for it.

Two documents the README references are **missing**: `v2/_PLAN.md` and `v2/_SETUP-FIREBASE.md`. `v2/assets/oa-alert-match.js` already fixes /lit/'s worst maintenance liability: it is a **dual-mode UMD file** loaded by the browser *and* `createRequire`d by `v2/_scraper/alerts-mailer.mjs`, so the in-form preview and the sent e-mail cannot disagree. Keep that pattern; do not regress to /lit/'s vendored copy.

## B. Target architecture

```
 ┌───────────────────────── BROWSER (static, no build step) ─────────────────────────┐
 │                                                                                    │
 │  /post-a-job  /submit-candidate ──► oa-firebase.js (compat SDK 10.12.5 from        │
 │        (signed-in, bounded doc)        gstatic; INERT while apiKey has 'PASTE_')   │
 │                                                                                    │
 │  /feedback  (no sign-in) ──► client-side JPEG compression → data-URL images        │
 │                                                                                    │
 │  /jobs /candidates /placements /recent-faculty /universities /previous-markets     │
 │        └─ fetch data/<set>.json + <set>-meta.json  ──► oa-list.js:                 │
 │              sel{} Sets ─► one filter pass ─► cross-filter counts ─► card list     │
 │        └─ fetch recent.json + recent-counts.json  (the "new this week" view)       │
 │        └─ fetch changelog.json  (What's new + alert preview)                       │
 │                                                                                    │
 │  /alerts (signed-in) ──► users/{uid}/alerts/{id}, users/{uid}/testEmails/{id}      │
 └───────────────┬──────────────────────────────────────────────┬─────────────────────┘
                 │ writes                                       │ reads (static HTTP)
                 ▼                                              │
 ┌──────────── FIRESTORE (project: OA's own) ────────────┐      │
 │ jobSubmissions/{id}      status:'pending' pinned      │      │
 │ candidateSubmissions/{id}                             │      │
 │ feedback/{id}            create-from-anyone, bounded  │      │
 │ paperless queues stamped by the Actions, never client │      │
 │ users/{uid}/{profile,alerts,testEmails}               │      │
 │ registeredUsers/{uid}    {t} only, public count()     │      │
 └───────────────┬───────────────────────────────────────┘      │
                 │ Admin SDK (FIREBASE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT)         │
                 ▼                                              │
 ┌──────────── GITHUB ACTIONS (cron, concurrency-grouped) ──────┴──────────────────┐
 │ oa-jobs-build.yml       */20  read pending → jobs-model → WRITE data/ FIRST →   │
 │ oa-candidates-build.yml       stamp Firestore → e-mail submitter → git commit   │
 │ oa-alerts-mail.yml      daily  collectionGroup('alerts') → oa-alert-match.js →  │
 │ oa-alerts-test.yml      */15   SMTP; per-stream high-water marks; commits none  │
 │ oa-feedback-mail.yml    */10   forward + submitter ack; then applyResolutions()  │
 │                                over _feedback-resolutions/*.md                   │
 │ oa-feedback-log.yml     */15   mirror feedback docs into a PRIVATE repo          │
 │ oa-checks.yml           push/PR  offline selftests, no network                   │
 └───────────────┬─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                 │ git push origin HEAD:master  (plain fast-forward, rebase-and-retry)
                 ▼
 ┌──────────── THIS REPOSITORY (public) ─────────────────────────────────────────┐
 │ v2/data/*.json committed → GitHub Pages redeploys → the pages above read it    │
 │ v2/_feedback-resolutions/<TICKET>.md  (public record of fixes; closes tickets) │
 └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

Two invariants carried from /lit/: **the browser never writes the served data** (only Firestore), and **the Action writes the dataset before stamping Firestore** so a crash re-processes idempotently instead of losing a submission.

## C. The reusable `/lit/` machinery, subsystem by subsystem

All `/lit/` paths below are relative to `/home/user/konstantinosStouras.github.io/`.

### C.1 Static-JSON data layer — **adapt (structure verbatim, field names rewritten)**

| Piece | Where | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| `writeJson` — `JSON.stringify(data)` **minified, deterministic key order** | `lit/_scraper/build-data.mjs:2906` | **Lift verbatim.** Determinism is the whole point: unchanged data ⇒ identical bytes ⇒ no commit ⇒ no Pages redeploy. |
| Atomic write (`.tmp-${pid}` + rename, 10-try backoff over EPERM/EBUSY/EACCES/ENOTEMPTY/EEXIST) | `lit/_scraper-workingpapers/ingest-submissions.mjs:487` | **Lift verbatim** for any writer that can race a reader. |
| `publicRow(p)` — destructure `_`-prefixed internals off at the serialisation boundary | `build-data.mjs:2642` | **Lift the convention.** OA's equivalent already exists as `PUBLIC_FIELDS` + `publicRow()` in `v2/_scraper/jobs-model.mjs` — an allow-list, which is stronger. Keep the allow-list. |
| Registry (`_registry.json` = `{regKey: 'YYYY-MM-DD'}`), `regKey()`, `updateRegistry()` with the first-run / `MASS_INFLUX=2000` / `SEED_COUNT=40` baselining and the **empty-string "seen but not news"** value | `build-data.mjs:556, 2418‑2447` | **Adapt.** This is the general answer to "when did this row first appear" without adding a field to every row, and the empty-string baseline is what stops the sheet import reading as 220 brand-new postings on day one. |
| `buildRecent` (90-day window, `RECENT_CAP=1000`) + `buildRecentCounts` (uncapped `{generated,windowDays,total,days:{key:{day:n}}}`) | `build-data.mjs:2559, 2594` | **Adapt, both or neither.** The lesson: ship a *capped rows* file for display and an *uncapped tiny tally* for the headline number, and make **every writer** of a dataset rewrite both. |
| `_chunked-json.mjs` (48 MiB parts, `writeChunkedJson` deletes stale higher parts) | `lit/_scraper/_chunked-json.mjs` (134 lines) | **Drop.** OA's largest dataset is ~2,400 rows / 80 KB. The 100 MiB push limit is not reachable. |
| Manifest `sources.json` (array of `{key,name,file,count,…}`) + `registerExtraSources` | `lit/data/sources.json`, `index.html:1576` | **Rewrite as a facet manifest.** OA has one file per dataset, not per source; what it needs from the manifest is the pre-computed facet counts and totals — which `v2/data/jobs-meta.json` already is. |
| Lazy sources (`neededNativeKeys`/`neededExtraKeys`/`loadExtraSource`/`extraState`/`afterSourceArrived` 700 ms coalescer), manifest-derived denominators, `?db=1` SQLite path | `index.html:2034‑2368`, `lit/_SQLITE-POC.md` | **Drop entirely.** These exist for 580k rows across 60 files. One `fetch` of one file is the OA case. |

### C.2 Result-list UI — **lift the pattern, rewrite the domain**

The whole of `/lit/index.html`'s list is driven by one mutable `sel` object (line 1283) of `Set`s, one `Array.filter` pass in `applyFilters()` (3388), then `renderPage()` (4003) → `renderCardList()` (3976).

**Lift near-verbatim:**
- The searchable multi-select trio: `pinSelectedFirst` (3296), `fillCustomSelect` (3303), `toggleDrop` (3317), `filterDrop` (3338), `selectItem` (3347) + the document-level outside-click (3363) and Escape (3371) handlers. ~60 lines, generic over a `data-type` attribute and `sel[type]`. The canonical DOM is `.filter-group > label + .custom-select[data-type] > .custom-select-trigger + .custom-select-dropdown > (.custom-select-search + .custom-select-items) + .chips`.
- The chip layer: `renderChips` (1430), `removeChip` (1421), `addTextChip` (1390), `addChipFromCard` (1512). **The whole chip removes the filter**, the `×` is decorative; `@keyframes chipIn` scales 0.85→1 in 0.15 s.
- Dual-mode text inputs: live filtering on a 150 ms debounce (`debounceSearch`, 4526, guarded by `allPapers.length > 0`) **and** Enter-to-chip (`onkeydown` calling `addTextChip`), with `autocomplete=off autocapitalize=off autocorrect=off spellcheck=false data-lpignore data-1p-ignore data-bwignore` to suppress password-manager overlays.
- Matching + escaping: `textMatch` (4368 — substring, or `\b…\b` word/phrase when the query is `"quoted"`), `nameFold` (4388, NFD diacritic strip with an ASCII fast path), `authorMatch` (4398, prefix-of-a-name-part), and the escaping trio `esc` / `escAttr` (for values inside `onclick="fn('…')"`) / `escHtmlAttr` (for `value="…"`) / `safeUrl` (4431, http(s)-only + percent-encodes `"'<>`).
- The CSS blocks: `.filters-bar`/`.filters-row`/`.filter-group` (129‑165), `.custom-select*` (168‑179), `.chip*` (180‑193), `.results-bar` + `.sort-control` (201‑205), the `.papers-list`/`.paper-card` border-collapse trick that makes a stack read as one rounded panel (207‑216), `.tag`/badge pills (224‑263), the colour-coded toggle panels (272‑307), `.empty-state`/`.loading`/`.spinner` (336‑340), and the three media blocks (347‑361, 401‑452) — including the ≥16 px input rule that stops iOS zooming on focus. Re-map `--navy` etc. to the OA palette in §A.1.
- **The reciprocity rule** from `paperCardHTML` (4080‑4134): *every* tag, badge, name and year on a card is a click-to-filter affordance calling the same `add*Chip` the filter bar uses. For OA this maps to institution / country / rank / field / deadline-bucket / year tags.
- `toggleFilterPanel` (3514) with `localStorage['litFiltersCollapsed']` persistence and the delegated click that makes the collapsed bar itself clickable.
- Lazy, memoised card toggles (`togAbs` 4136, `togBib` 4143 with its `el.dataset.filled` guard and `dataset.bib` stash) — for OA: the full job description, the "comments on posting", the BibTeX-equivalent (a copyable citation is not needed; a copyable *share link* is).

**Adapt:** `crossFilter(excludeType)` (3224) — the idea (recount every dropdown under all *other* filters, applying the flag-only filters unconditionally so chained counts stay honest) is exactly right; the implementation is a hand-unrolled per-domain chain. `v2/assets/oa-list.js`'s `passing(skipKey)` over a declarative filter spec is the correct generalisation. **[verified in repo]**

**Rewrite:** `applyFilters` (its 15-clause emptiness test, editor/area/SE/AE clauses, `ensureScopeSources()`); the sort comparator (3467‑3475) — OA wants deadline / posted / institution / rank, keeping the `statusRank` (3386) idea that rows in a special state float above equal-date rows rather than sinking on an empty field; the results-bar denominator (`scopeCount` counted inline during the pass — OA's denominator is simply the dataset total).

**Drop:** `RENDER_FIRST=250`/`RENDER_MORE=500` chunking (one `innerHTML` write for 2,400 cards is fine), `recentMode` as a **parallel render path** (`renderRecent` 3832 bypasses `applyFilters` entirely and every chip mutator has to branch on it, at 1426/1448/1459/1617/3358) — make "newest first" a sort mode inside the one loop, and `body.compact` sticky-condensing.

**Deep links.** /lit/ URL-syncs only the *focal* filter (`?author=`, `?citedby=`, `?citedbyauthor=`) via `applyAuthorDeepLink` (4785) / `applyCitedByDeepLink` (4805) / `litSyncCitedByUrl` (2011) with `history.replaceState`. **For OA this is the wrong trade** — the whole `sel` should serialise, because the Universities map deep-links into every other page (`?filterA=`, `?filterD=`, `?filterE=`, `?filterF=`) and those 144×5 = 720 links must keep working. `litFilterSig()` (3582) already computes a stable sorted signature of the entire selection and is the ready-made basis.

### C.3 Accounts / sign-in — **lift near-verbatim, minus ORCID**

The whole feature is one IIFE at `lit/index.html:5158‑8209` on the **compat** CDN SDK 10.12.5 (`firebase-{app,auth,firestore}-compat.js`; `database-compat` only for the separate presence app).

**Lift near-verbatim:**

  `var ACCOUNTS_ENABLED = !!(FB_CONFIG.apiKey && FB_CONFIG.apiKey.indexOf('PASTE_') === -1 && window.firebase && firebase.auth && firebase.firestore); if (!ACCOUNTS_ENABLED) return;`

One modal, two modes.

Together they enforce **"a signed-in user is never shown the sign-in modal again"**. Rename the keys (`oaAuthHint`, `oaProfHint`).
- `acctHash`/`acctAvatarSeed`/`acctAvatarUrl` (5477‑5502) — a 5×5 mirrored-cell identicon as a `data:image/svg+xml,` URL. No avatar hosting.
- The `onAuthStateChanged` skeleton (8088‑8198): hint write/clear, listener teardown + state reset + per-session guard reset, the best-effort `registeredUsers/{uid}.set({t:serverTime()},{merge:true})` marker behind a `lastMarkedUid` guard, listener attach with warn-only error callbacks, the signed-out overlay sweep, the `pendingAcctActions` drain, the hash-link call. Plus `onData()` (8052) as the **single** snapshot fan-out.
- Edit-profile: `#acctProfileOverlay` markup (4873‑4946) minus the ORCID/merge blocks, `acctOpenProfile` (6141) **including the `pendingProfileOpen` deferral** (a modal opened before its snapshot renders blank fields whose Save wipes the profile), and `acctSaveProfile` (6694): first+last required, e-mail regex, website gets `https://` prepended, `profileDoc().set(prof,{merge:true})` + `updateProfile({displayName})`, "Saved." then auto-close at 700 ms.

Its structure transfers unchanged: reuse-or-create the default app, hint-cache paint, `loadExtras()` = one `profile/main` `.get()` + two `count()` aggregates (3 reads per page view), `data-acct-toggle`/`data-acct-menu`/`data-acct-signout` attributes with `addEventListener` instead of inline `onclick`, `injectStyles()` behind a single `<style id>` guard. The host page must supply `<div id="acctControl" class="acct-control"></div>`.

Google + e-mail/password does not need it.

> **REVERSED, 2026‑08‑16 (owner).** The premise of that last sentence did not
> survive the build: `AUTH_PROVIDERS` ships as `['google','orcid','password']`,
> so ORCID's OIDC — and its missing e-mail — is exactly what OA offers. `normOrcid`
> (checksum and all), the `oidc.orcid` provider, `accountKeys` detection and a
> merge are all present in `v2/assets/oa-accounts.js`. The rest of the ORCID
> layer stays dropped: nothing here matches an author to papers, so
> `orcidMatchName`, `backfillOrcidAuthorName` and `litMyPubCount` have no
> subject, and the iD is read from the sign-in's own OIDC `sub` rather than
> through a second implicit OAuth flow.
>
> The owner's requirement is also WIDER than /lit/'s: two Gmail addresses are
> two accounts as surely as Google-and-ORCID is, so **any** two accounts merge,
> not only an ORCID-only duplicate. That is why the flow differs from /lit/'s
> localStorage hand-over: a **job posting** is a top-level `jobSubmissions`
> document owned by a `uid` field, so once the duplicate sign-in is deleted
> nobody can ever reach it again. The merge therefore signs the kept account in
> on a **second Firebase app** and proves both at once, handing the postings
> over while the account that owns them is still there. See the comment above
> `openMerge`.

### C.4 E-mail alerts — **lift the engine, generalise the streams**

`/lit/` splits this three ways: the modal in `index.html` (7112‑7575), the mailer `lit/_scraper/alerts-mailer.mjs` (1,262 lines, zero runtime deps beyond lazily-imported `firebase-admin` + `nodemailer`), and `lit/changelog.json` as the single source read by three consumers.

**Lift near-verbatim (none of it knows anything about papers):**
- The delivery skeleton in `run()` (697‑822): credentials guard → load items → `collectionGroup('alerts').get()` (Admin SDK bypasses rules, no composite index needed) → per-alert evaluate → send → `doc.ref.set(update,{merge:true})`.
- Windowing: `DAY_MS`, `dayStart(d)` (floor to UTC midnight), `windowStartFor(last, created, now)` (643 — `dayStart(last)`, else `max(dayStart(created) - DAY_MS, dayStart(now) - 31*DAY_MS)`), `FREQ_MIN_DAYS = {immediate:0, daily:0, weekly:6.5, monthly:27.5}` with the **`-0.05` cron-jitter slack**, `toDate(v)` (664) unwrapping Firestore Timestamps. **The day-flooring is a bug fix, not decoration:** item dates parse to 00:00Z while marks are mid-day timestamps, so a strict `>` dropped everything dated *today* and an alert created today never saw today's items.
- The e-mail chrome: `esc`, `footerText`, `footerHtml`, `emailShell(headerLabel, inner, banner)` (412‑454) and the `opts = {subjectPrefix, noteText, bannerHtml}` convention that lets the test path reuse the production templates. Recipient regex `/^[^@\s]+@[^@\s]+\.[^@\s]+$/`; `mkMsg` (760) with `from` = the site, `to` = recipient, `replyTo` = the subscriber, and the `List-Unsubscribe` header.
- **The website-updates alert, whole** — `changelog.json` (`{version, updates:[{id,date,title,summary,url}]}`, newest first), `loadChangelog()` (358), `evaluateFeatures()` (619+), `renderFeatureDigest()` (530), the **independent** `lastFeatureCheckedAt`/`lastFeatureSentAt` marks (falling back to the paper mark so enabling it never blasts history), and the three-consumer pattern: the About page list, the in-form live preview, the digest e-mail. *To announce something you add a changelog entry dated ~today; an entry dated in the past reaches nobody, so seeding history is safe.* This is the one of OA's four alert kinds that needs no redesign.
- The test-e-mail loop: the `users/{uid}/testEmails/{id}` queue, `sendTestEmails()` (831) with a 3-attempt-then-delete retry, `[Test]` prefix + banner, and its own 15-minute workflow on a separate concurrency group.
- The maintainer modes: `--announce` (513/1193, broadcast to `criteria.features` recipients, **deduped by lower-cased address**, deliberately does *not* touch the feature high-water mark), `--rewind` (920, clears marks on alerts created within 3 days), `--scan` (1170), and the `--selftest` harness shape (a plain `ok(name, cond)` counter, 91 assertions, no deps, exit 1 on failure).

**Adapt — the subscription UI** (`emptyCriteria`/`fromCriteria`/`normalizeCriteria`/`critCount`/`alertHasIntent`/`defaultAlertName` 7112‑7221, `litAlertSave`/`litAlertSendTest` 7223‑7359, `renderExistingAlerts` 7516 with its pause/edit/delete, the `onSnapshot`-driven re-render, `.alert-*`/`.apm-*` CSS 695‑769). The modal **pre-fills the criteria from the page's current filters** (`captureCurrentFilters`) and shows a **live example e-mail** at the bottom — keep both; they are why subscribers understand what they signed up for. The alert *name is the subject line* and the field is labelled as such.

**Rewrite — the architectural gap.** /lit/ hard-codes exactly **two** streams per alert (papers + features), each with its own bespoke mark pair and its own `if` block in `run()`, and `evaluateAlert`/`evaluateFeatures` are 90 % the same function. OA needs **four** (jobs, candidates, news, updates). Collapse to a table before adding the third:

```js
const STREAMS = [
  { key:'jobs',       file:'data/jobs.json',       dateField:'posted',  hasIntent, matches, render, checked:'lastJobsCheckedAt',  sent:'lastJobsSentAt' },
  { key:'candidates', file:'data/candidates.json', dateField:'posted',  … },
  { key:'news',       file:'data/news.json',       dateField:'date',    … },
  { key:'updates',    file:'changelog.json',       dateField:'date',    … },
];
```
with one `evaluateStream(alert, items, now, stream)` and one loop, each stream advancing **only its own** mark and only on its own successful send.

**Do not copy:** the vendored journal sets and the hand-copied `textMatch`/`authorMatch` in the mailer (the file's own header says "keep them in sync"; nothing detects drift) — **[verified in repo]** `v2/assets/oa-alert-match.js` already replaces this with a dual-mode UMD file used by both sides. Nor the third copy of the templates in `renderAlertPreview()` (7438); render the preview through the *same* renderer where possible.

### C.5 Feedback → resolution loop — **lift near-verbatim**

One static page writes one bounded Firestore doc; two mailers deliver it; a repo directory closes the loop; a private repo mirrors it.

- **Client** (`lit/feedback/index.html`, 1,147 lines, one IIFE from 437). **Lift verbatim:** `compressImage()` (513‑538) — canvas downscale to `MAX_EDGE=1400`, **white fill first** (flattens alpha for JPEG), quality ladder `[0.72, 0.6, 0.48]` breaking at ≤500 KB, with `MAX_IMAGES=5` and `TOTAL_BUDGET=900*1024` counted on the **data-URL string length**. That is the whole "no file storage needed" trick: images ride inside the doc, under Firestore's ~1 MB cap. And `genTicket()` (588‑595) — `'LIT-' + YYMMDD + '-' + 4 chars` — change the prefix to `OA-` and the mailer's validating regex with it.
- **Doc shape** (606‑619): `{text, images[], name, email, uid, ticket, page, url: document.referrer.slice(0,500), ua: navigator.userAgent.slice(0,400), forwarded:false, status:'new', createdAt}`. Server-added later: `forwarded`, `status`, `forwardedAt`, `forwardedBy`, `ackSent`, `ackAt`, `resolution`, `resolutionUrl`, `resolutionHash`, `resolutionSent`, `resolvedAt`, `resolvedBy`, `closedAt`.
- **Maintainer inbox** on the same page (645‑851): Open/Closed/All tabs, screenshots on top with a lightbox, message below, **Mark complete & reply** (prompt → `{status:'closed', resolution, closedAt}` → `mailto:` with the address deliberately *not* percent-encoded per RFC 6068), Reopen, Delete. Authorisation is the rule; the client check only decides whether to render.
- **Batch mailer** `lit/_scraper/feedback-mailer.mjs` (565 lines). **Lift near-verbatim:** `dataUrlToAttachment` (89), `renderFeedbackEmail` (109) with its metadata rows, `renderSubmitterEmail` (155 — returns `null` when there is no valid reply-to, which is the single guard for "anonymous cannot be confirmed"), the query `where('forwarded','==',false).limit(50)` sorted oldest-first **in memory** (no orderBy ⇒ no composite index), and the asymmetric failure handling: a maintainer-copy failure `continue`s (both e-mails retry, guarded from doubling only by `ackSent`); an ack failure is logged and never un-forwards.
- **Resolutions** (`lit/_feedback-resolutions/`): one `<TICKET>.md` per resolved ticket, front matter `ticket:` (or `doc:`) + optional **host-validated** `url:`, body e-mailed verbatim. **Lift verbatim:** `parseResolutionFile` (190), `resolutionHashOf` (225 — sha256 of ticket+url+body, first 16 hex), `renderResolutionEmail` (234), `applyResolutions` (280) with its **write-before-stamp** ordering (close the doc, *then* e-mail, then stamp `resolutionSent`), and `resolutionFiles()` (269 — `.md` only, excluding `README.md` and `_`-prefixed). Files stay in place as the public record; an unchanged file is skipped forever; **editing one re-applies and re-e-mails**.
- **Instant delivery** — the Cloud Function `lit/_functions/functions/index.js` `forwardFeedbackOnCreate` (2nd gen `onDocumentCreated`, `secrets:[SMTP_USER,SMTP_PASS]`, `defineString` for the rest, `setGlobalOptions({region, maxInstances:5})`, early-return on `forwarded===true`, **never rethrows** on send failure so the batch mailer retries). `REGION` must match the Firestore location. Its renderers are a hand-maintained **copy** (`feedback-render.js`) because a Functions deploy bundles only its own directory. **Optional for OA** — the 10-minute batch mailer is the always-on path; add the Function only if instant delivery matters.
- **Private GitHub mirror** `lit/_scraper/feedback-github-log.mjs` (360 lines) — **lift in full**; `syncSubmission`/`indexEntry`/`buildIndex` are pure functions over a plain doc object, only the Firestore read in `main()` is site-specific. Layout `feedback/<docId>/{feedback.md, feedback.json, screenshot-N.jpg}` + `feedback/INDEX.md` + `index.json`. `buildIndex` is **deterministic** (no generated-at stamp), which is what makes the workflow's `git diff --staged --quiet` a genuine no-op. Folders are named after the doc id, so the index is the only ticket → folder map.

**The standard workflow this buys:** read the ticket from the private log (`feedback/INDEX.md` → its folder), ship the fix, and add `v2/_feedback-resolutions/<TICKET>.md` in the **same** change — the submitter's closure e-mail then goes out automatically on merge.

### C.6 Submission ingest — **adapt (the ordering is the design)**

Reference: `lit/_scraper-workingpapers/ingest-submissions.mjs` (872 lines).

**Lift the `run()` order verbatim** (653‑847): (a) no-op immediately if `FIREBASE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT`/`GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` is unset; (b) read `where('status','==','pending').limit(LIMIT)` sorted oldest-`createdAt`-first; (c) `--scan` prints and exits; (d) load the current dataset into an in-memory map; (e) per doc: route → resolve → decide with a **pure** function; (f) `if (DRY_RUN) return` before any write; (g) **write the dataset**; (h) only then stamp each Firestore doc; (i) e-mail, best-effort, in its own try/catch. Also lift the `--dry-run` / `--scan` / `--limit=N` trio and `regroupAndWrite` (420) as the "rewrite the whole dataset from an in-memory Map" shape.

**Outcome vocabulary to adapt:** `added` | `duplicate` | `review` | `rejected`, plus the in-memory transients `retry` (transient API failure — leave `pending`) and `notfound` (increment `tries`, stamp `lastTriedAt`, leave pending until `SUB_MAX_AGE_DAYS`, then reject). Stamp `status, processedAt, reason, detail` and keep `notified`/`notifiedAt` **separate** so an e-mail failure never un-stamps the outcome.

**Rewrite for OA:** the routing/resolution layer is entirely paper-specific (`routeSubmission`, `urlToDoi`, Crossref/OpenAlex resolution, `catalogAuthorIndex`). OA's equivalent is much simpler and already exists as `rowFromSubmission()` in `v2/_scraper/jobs-model.mjs` **[verified in repo]**. Keep the one principle: **never trust submitter-typed metadata straight into the dataset** — sanitise through the shared model (`text()`, `url()` http(s)-only, `day()`, `pickList()` against the allow-lists) so a hand-import row and a live row are byte-identical.

### C.7 GitHub Actions idiom — **lift verbatim**

Five parts, present in `lit-update-data.yml` and `lit-paper-submissions.yml`:
1. `on:` = cron (**off-boundary minutes**, e.g. `3,13,23,33,43,53` / `7,27,47`, to dodge schedule throttling) + `workflow_dispatch` with typed `inputs` (`dry_run`, `scan`) + optionally a `push:` with a `paths:` filter naming the pipeline files.
2. `concurrency: {group: <dataset>-${{ github.ref }}, cancel-in-progress: false}` — **one group per data directory**, shared by every job that writes it.
3. `permissions: contents: write` (or `contents: read` for mailers, which push nothing).
4. Master-only commit: `if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/master'`, `git config user.name github-actions[bot]` / `41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com`, `git add <dir>`, **`if git diff --cached --quiet; then echo 'nothing to commit'; exit 0; fi`**, commit.
5. A 3–5 attempt push loop. Two flavours: **sole-owner replay** (`cp -r <dir> /tmp/x-ours` before the loop; on rejection `git fetch`, `git reset --hard origin/$REF`, restore from `/tmp`, re-add) — correct *because* the concurrency group makes our copy authoritative; and **merge-the-tip** (a mixed `git reset origin/$REF`, never `--hard` which drops code commits, never `--soft` which silently reverts them). **OA is single-writer per dataset — use the replay flavour, or the simpler `git pull --rebase` retry already in `oa-jobs-build.yml`.**

**Do not copy** the `--apply-only --merge-cache` replay or the live-site `meta.json` `lastPull` poll + `POST /repos/…/pages/builds` self-heal — both exist because several independent jobs write one directory and Pages deploys were observed to fail silently. Revisit only if OA sees a stale deploy.

## D. Data model for the new site

### D.1 Conventions (carried from /lit/, tightened by the v2 prototype)

- One directory per site (`v2/data/`), one JSON **array** file per dataset, plus a small `-meta.json` per dataset, plus the shared `recent.json` / `recent-counts.json` / `changelog.json`.
- **Files beginning with `_` are internal state and never served** (`_registry.json`). *Note: GitHub Pages runs Jekyll by default here and skips `_`-prefixed paths — which is convenient for `_registry.json` but means `v2/_scraper/`, `v2/_firestore.rules` and `v2/_feedback-resolutions/` are also unpublished. Add `.nojekyll` only if you want them served, and re-check this rule if you do.*
- Every writer of a dataset rewrites **all** of its derived files in the same pass.
- A **published-fields allow-list** governs serialisation. Nothing outside it reaches `data/` — that is how submitter and department-chair e-mail addresses stay out of a public repository.
- Values are typed (unlike /lit/'s all-strings convention): the sheet's junk (`"200"`, `"100"`, `"2023-24"`) must be coerced or rejected at import, not carried.

### D.2 Jobs — `v2/data/jobs.json` **[verified in repo]**

`PUBLIC_FIELDS` (`v2/_scraper/jobs-model.mjs:22`), in write order:

```jsonc
{
  "id": "2026-cuhk-business-school-20250806",   // `${year}-${slug(institution)}-${YYYYMMDD}`
  "year": 2026,                                  // number
  "posted": "2025-08-06",                        // YYYY-MM-DD
  "institution": "CUHK Business School",         // ≤160
  "department": "Department of Decisions, Operations and Technology", // ≤220
  "type": "Business School",                     // TYPES = ['Business School','University']
  "levels": ["Assistant Professor","Other Ranks"],           // subset of LEVELS (5)
  "applyBy": "December 31, 2025. We advise candidates…",     // ≤400, the human string
  "applyByDate": "2025-12-31",                   // machine date, drives the Deadline bucket
  "comments": "",                                // ≤1200 (the INFORMS-interview note)
  "country": "Hong Kong",                        // ≤60, normalised
  "adUrl": "https://drive.google.com/open?id=…", "adLabel": "link to Job ad",
  "postedAtUrl": "http://www.operationsacademia.org/", "postedAtLabel": "Operations Academia",
  "furtherInfoUrl": "http://www.operationsacademia.org/universities?filterA=CUHK Business School",
  "characteristics": ["Research seminars","PhD","Undergrad","Masters","MBA","Exec Ed"], // 6 allowed
  "featured": true,
  "source": "sheet-import",                      // or "submission"
  "addedAt": "2025-08-06T08:42:07Z",
  "ref": "<firestore doc id>"                    // present on submitted rows; mergeRows replaces by it
}
```

Deliberately **absent**: every e-mail address, the submitter's and chair's names, the raw checkbox sentence. Note `Masters` is a first-class characteristic here although the old `jobsData` fan-out (`HasSeminars?`…`HasUndergrad?`) had no column for it — the raw checkbox answer does, so the import recovers it.

Model helpers to keep: `text()`, `url()` (http(s) or `''` — `javascript:`/`data:` dropped, not repaired), `day()`, `pickList(v, allowed)`, `slug()`, `jobId()`, `rowFromSubmission()`, `publicRow()`, `mergeRows(existing, fresh, remove)` (replace by `ref`, idempotent), `displayOrder()`, `buildMeta()`, `serialise()`, `isoDay`/`isoStamp`/`longDate`.

### D.3 The facet manifest — `v2/data/jobs-meta.json` **[verified in repo]**

```json
{ "generated":"2026-08-15T15:33:47.133Z", "count":80,
  "years":{"2026":12,"2025":67,"2020":1},
  "types":{"Business School":57,"University":23},
  "levels":{…}, "countries":{…}, "characteristics":{…},
  "featured":1, "newestPosted":"2025-08-13" }
```

This replaces /lit/'s `sources.json` + `meta.json`. It lets the filter bar paint its option lists with counts before the rows arrive, and `generated`/`newestPosted` are the poll targets if a deploy self-heal is ever needed.

### D.4 The other datasets (to be built; shapes derived from §A.2)

**`candidates.json`** — `{id, year, posted, first, last, name, affiliation, position, researchAreas[], cvUrl, researchSummaryUrl, webUrl, informsDays[], addedAt, ref}`. Notes: prefer the *typed* CV link over the Drive upload (as the display tab's formula does), keep `informsDays` as the cleaned day list (drop `Saturday`, expand legacy session codes), and **do not publish `email`** — the old display tab did publish it; the new page should offer a mailto only if the candidate opts in. Approval must become a real field (`published: true`), not a typed `OK`.

**`placements.json`** (Confirmed Placements) — `{id, year, first, last, name, phdInstitution, undergradInstitution, joiningInstitution, joiningPosition, note, webUrl, addedAt, ref}`. The import must **split** `Assistant Professor (INSEAD)` into `joiningPosition` + `joiningInstitution` for the older rows so the two eras render alike, and must not emit the leading `", "`.

**`faculty.json`** (Recent Faculty) — `{id, year, name, phdInstitution, undergradInstitution, placement, placementDepartment, webUrl, phdIsBusinessSchool, joiningIsBusinessSchool, addedAt}`. `isOK` becomes `published`. The 22 hand-appended display rows and the 8 lifted helper rows have no raw counterpart — import from the **display** tab for this dataset.

**`universities.json`** — `{key, name, school, department, address, lat, lng, facultyUrl}`. `key` = the current `University/ Institution` join value, **unchanged**, because 720 existing deep links and every job row's `furtherInfoUrl` depend on it. The five per-row anchor columns become computed links in the page, not stored HTML.

**`jobs-archive.json`** (Past job postings) — the same shape as `jobs.json` with `source:"sheet-import-archive"`; import from the **display** tab (93 rows), since its raw tab holds only 51. `characteristics` is `NA` throughout and should be `[]`.

### D.5 Recency files

- **`v2/data/_registry.json`** — `{rowId: "YYYY-MM-DD"}`, unserved. Seeded by the migration with **empty strings** for every imported row except the newest ~40, so the import does not read as 220 new postings on day one.
- **`v2/data/recent.json`** — dated rows across *all* datasets, newest first, capped (a few hundred is ample), each carrying `dataset` + the display fields the alert e-mail and the "new this week" view need.
- **`v2/data/recent-counts.json`** — `{generated, windowDays, total, days:{"<dataset>":{"YYYY-MM-DD":n}}}`, uncapped, ~1 KB. **The headline "N new this week" number is read from here, never by counting the capped rows** — that under-reporting is the exact bug /lit/ shipped and had to fix.
- **`v2/changelog.json`** **[verified in repo]** — `{version, note, updates:[{id, date, title, summary, url}]}`, newest first. Already seeded with the `own-job-postings-table` entry.

**Bucket fields are derived at read time, never stored.** The sheet's `Date posted` / `Deadline` columns were formulas whose branches are unobservable; the page recomputes them from `posted` and `applyByDate` (`v2/assets/oa-list.js`'s `DERIVE`).

## E. Firebase surface

### E.1 Collections

| Path | Written by | Read by | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `jobSubmissions/{id}` | `/post-a-job` (signed-in) | ingest Action (Admin SDK), submitter's own doc, admin | `status:'pending'` pinned by the rule; **[verified in repo]** rule already present |
| `candidateSubmissions/{id}` | `/submit-candidate` | same | to be added, same shape |
| `feedback/{id}` | `/feedback` (**no sign-in**) | mailer, GitHub-log mirror, admin inbox | images are base64 data URLs inside the doc |
| `users/{uid}/profile/main` | the account modal | the owner | `{firstName,lastName,affiliation,website,email,updatedAt}` + any feature fields, always `{merge:true}` |
| `users/{uid}/alerts/{id}` | the alerts modal | the mailer via `collectionGroup('alerts')` | `{name, recipient, from, frequency, enabled, criteria, createdAt, updatedAt}` + per-stream `last*CheckedAt`/`last*SentAt` |
| `users/{uid}/testEmails/{id}` | "Send me a test e-mail" | the 15-min test pass (delivers then **deletes**) | `{…criteria, test:true, attempts}` |
| `registeredUsers/{uid}` | `onAuthStateChanged`, best-effort | a public `count()` on a stats tile | `{t}` only, no PII |

**Not carried over:** `publicLists`, `paperSubmissions`. (`accountKeys` **is** carried over after all — see the reversal note in C.3. `accountKeys/{key}` holds `{uid, t}` under `orcid:<iD>` / `email:<sha256>`, is `get`-only for anyone signed in and never listable, and is a hint that two accounts are one person — never an authorisation.)

**Alert `criteria` for OA** — one `topics` array (`['jobs','candidates','news','updates']`, already the vocabulary in `v2/assets/oa-alert-match.js` **[verified in repo]**) plus per-topic filter Sets mirroring the page's `sel` (country, type, level, characteristic, year, institution/free text), plus `allJobs`-style short-circuits. A save needs **any one intent** (`alertHasIntent`).

### E.2 Rules (`v2/_firestore.rules`) **[verified in repo]** — present, needs the candidate queue added

Shape already in place: `signedIn()`, `isOwner(uid)`, `isAdmin()`, `str(field,max)`, `list(field,max)` helpers; `jobSubmissions` bounded create + owner read/update + admin delete; `feedback` bounded create-from-anyone + admin read/update/delete; `users/{uid}/{document=**}` owner-only; `profiles/{uid}` owner-only; `registeredUsers/{uid}` public read + owner `{t}`-only write + `delete: if false`; a final `match /{document=**} { allow read, write: if false; }`.

Rules discipline to carry from `lit/_firestore.rules`:
- **`keys().hasOnly([...])` + per-field `.size()` caps + `status == 'pending'` pinned** on every client-created queue doc. Consequence: **adding a field to the client write breaks every create with `permission-denied` until the rules are republished** — mitigate as `lit/feedback/index.html` does, with a one-shot retry in the legacy shape on `err.code === 'permission-denied'`.
- **`get` vs `read`.** `read` = get + list. Any collection where a document id is a secret (a share link) or a field is harvestable must grant `get` only.
- `registeredUsers` is **deliberately publicly enumerable** — `count()` is evaluated under the same read rules as the query, so there is no count-without-list. It holds uids + a coarse timestamp and nothing else. If that is unacceptable, use a Function-incremented counter doc instead.
- `isAdmin()` must require `request.auth.token.email_verified == true` alongside the address.
- Rules cannot iterate list elements, so there is **no per-image byte cap** on feedback. Documented follow-ups: App Check (`request.app != null`), requiring anonymous sign-in, and a GCP billing budget.

### E.3 Auth providers and the inert gate

- SDK: four `<script src="https://www.gstatic.com/firebasejs/10.12.5/firebase-{app,auth,firestore}-compat.js">` tags — plain non-module compat builds, no npm, no build step. **[verified in repo]** `v2/assets/oa-firebase.js` loads them lazily and exposes a `ready()` promise, which is better than /lit/'s four duplicated `FB_CONFIG` copies (main page, `lit-acct-nav.js`, analytics, feedback, plus a fifth partial for presence). **Keep the single-module approach.**
- Providers: `['google','password']` to start. `PROVIDER_DEFS` supports `google`/`apple`/`github`/`orcid` (`new firebase.auth.GoogleAuthProvider()`, `new firebase.auth.OAuthProvider('apple.com')`, `new firebase.auth.GithubAuthProvider()`, `new firebase.auth.OAuthProvider('oidc.orcid')`), rendered from whatever is listed. **Keep the list in step with what is actually enabled in the console** or the button 500s.
- The gate: `apiKey.indexOf('PASTE_') === -1`. Everything — sign-in, the two forms, alerts, feedback — checks it first and degrades to an honest "not available yet" state. This is what lets the whole rebuild be committed and served before the project exists.

**Operator setup** (from `lit/_ACCOUNTS-SETUP.md`): create the project → Authentication → enable Email/Password + Google → Settings → Authorized domains → add `www.operationsacademia.org` **and** `operationsacademia.org` → Project settings → Web app → copy the config into `oa-firebase.js` (web configs are **not** secrets) → Firestore → create in production mode → publish `v2/_firestore.rules` (console paste, or `firebase deploy --only firestore:rules` from a directory holding `firebase.json`; note /lit/ keeps `firebase.json`/`.firebaserc` **beside** the rules because the CLI requires every referenced path inside the config's own directory) → commit. Reverting = put the `PASTE_` placeholders back.

## F. GitHub Actions surface

| Workflow | Cadence | `concurrency.group` | Permissions | Commits |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **`oa-checks.yml`** **[exists]** | push + PR on `v2/**` | — | `contents: read` | nothing |
| **`oa-jobs-build.yml`** **[exists]** | `7,27,47 * * * *` | `oa-jobs-data-${{ github.ref }}` | `contents: write` | `v2/data/` |
| `oa-candidates-build.yml` | `12,32,52 * * * *` | `oa-candidates-data-${{ github.ref }}` | `contents: write` | `v2/data/` |
| `oa-alerts-mail.yml` | `30 8 * * *` | `oa-alerts-mail` | `contents: read` | nothing |
| `oa-alerts-test.yml` | `*/15 * * * *` | `oa-alerts-test` | `contents: read` | nothing |
| `oa-feedback-mail.yml` | `3,13,23,33,43,53 * * * *` | `oa-feedback-mail` | `contents: read` | nothing (Firestore only) |
| `oa-feedback-log.yml` | `8,23,38,53 * * * *`, gated `if: vars.FEEDBACK_LOG_REPO != ''` | `oa-feedback-log` | `contents: read` | the **private** log repo |

Notes:
- **If two datasets share one directory they must share one concurrency group.** Simplest correct option for OA: put every `v2/data/` writer in **one** group, `oa-data-${{ github.ref }}`.
- `oa-checks.yml` already enforces three things worth keeping verbatim **[verified in repo]**: every `v2/assets/*.js` and `v2/_scraper/*.mjs` passes `node --check`; `selftest.mjs` runs; and a **secret-leak guard** that fails the build if any e-mail-shaped string appears anywhere under `v2/data/` or `BEGIN PRIVATE KEY` appears anywhere under `v2/`. Plus a Playwright `page-test.mjs` that asserts the page actually renders its data.
- `oa-jobs-build.yml` already runs `selftest.mjs` **twice** — before writing, and again against the file it is about to commit.
- Mailers use `npm install --no-save firebase-admin@12 nodemailer@6` and are a **clean no-op** (log a line, exit 0) until `FIREBASE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT` + `SMTP_USER` exist. A green run therefore does **not** prove mail was sent — verify with `--dry-run` (which still needs the Firebase secret).

**Secrets / variables:** `FIREBASE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT` (whole JSON; the only one required for the ingest) · `SMTP_HOST` (default `smtp.gmail.com`) / `SMTP_PORT` (465) / `SMTP_SECURE` / `SMTP_USER` / `SMTP_PASS` (a Gmail App Password) · `ALERTS_FROM`, `ALERTS_FROM_NAME`, `FEEDBACK_TO`, `CONTACT_EMAIL` · variable `FEEDBACK_LOG_REPO` + secret `FEEDBACK_LOG_TOKEN` (fine-grained PAT, Contents: write). The log-repo checkout must happen **after** `npm install`, so the credential is not on disk while third-party install scripts run.

**Branch protection:** the default branch may be protected against force-push and deletion **only**. "Require a pull request before merging" and "Require status checks" would reject every `GITHUB_TOKEN` push from these workflows and the site would silently stop updating. Nothing here force-pushes, deletes a branch, or pushes tags.

## G. Migration

### G.1 What moves, and from which tab

| Dataset | Import from | Rows | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| Jobs (current market) | Job Postings **raw** (`rawData`, 129) | 129 | The display tab is 49 submissions stale; raw is the truth. Re-derive `applyBy`, `characteristics`, the buckets. |
| Jobs (archive) | Past job postings **display** (93) | 93 | Its raw tab holds only 51; the display tab was accumulated by hand. |
| Candidates | Candidates **raw** (104) | 104 | 1:1 mirror; raw has the untransformed fields. |
| Placements | Confirmed Placements **raw** (173) | 173 | Includes the six curator-added columns. |
| Recent Faculty | Recent Faculty **display** (212) | 212 | 22 rows exist only there; `isOK` lives there. |
| Universities | `Universities` (144) | 144 | The only tab. |

**Total job rows ≈ 222** (129 current + 93 archive) — the "~220" in the brief.

### G.2 Import mechanics

1. **Export each tab to CSV** by hand (`File → Download → CSV` per tab). *The Drive connector used for the research could not export xlsx (`Operation is not implemented`) and the sandbox has no egress, so an automated pull was not possible; assume a manual export.*
2. Write **`v2/_scraper/import-sheet.mjs`**, a sibling of `build-jobs.mjs` that produces rows through the **same** `jobs-model.mjs` functions (`rowFromSubmission`-equivalent → `publicRow` → `mergeRows` → `serialise`). `jobs-model.mjs`'s own header already names this file as the intended second writer **[verified in repo]** — keeping one model is what stops "cards that render differently depending on when they were posted".
3. **Cleaning rules to encode in the importer** (all observed in the data):
   - `Job Market Year`: reject/repair `200`, `100`; map `2023-24` → `2024`.
   - Country: normalise `UK`/`United Kingdom` → one value, `United States`/`USA` → one, `Hong Kong SAR` → `Hong Kong`, `Shenzhen, China` / `China (Shanghai)` → `China` (keep the city in `department` or drop).
   - Dates: `12/1/12014` → `2014-12-01`; every date to ISO; `applyBy` keeps the human string, `applyByDate` the machine one; a missing date means "until filled", never a fabricated one.
   - Anchors → plain URLs (`adUrl`/`postedAtUrl`); the literal `"NA"` → `""`; the `Operations Academia` self-link fallback preserved as `postedAtUrl`+`postedAtLabel`.
   - Checkboxes → the `characteristics` allow-list (including `Masters`, which the old fan-out dropped).
   - Names: collapse the double spaces caused by trailing blanks in raw first names.
   - Placements: split `Assistant Professor (INSEAD)` into position + institution; never emit a leading `", "`.
   - **Approval**: `published: true` where the sheet says so (`isOK == 'ok'`, or the typed `OK` in the comments field), and a maintainer decision for the rest — do **not** silently publish the 49 never-displayed job rows without a review pass.
   - **Drop every e-mail address and personal name of submitters/chairs** at the allow-list boundary (`oa-checks.yml` will fail the build if one slips through).
4. **Seed `_registry.json`** in the same run: empty string for everything except the newest ~40 rows per dataset, so "recently added" and the first alerts e-mail are not a 220-row blast.
5. Re-run `selftest.mjs` and `page-test.mjs`; commit `v2/data/` in one migration commit.

### G.3 Dual run

Everything already lives under `/v2/` with `<meta name="robots" content="noindex,nofollow">`, the live pages untouched, and `v2/assets/oa-nav.js` carrying **absolute** hrefs because relative extensionless links break one directory down **[verified in repo]**. During the dual run:

- The Google Forms stay open and the sheets keep receiving submissions; the new `/v2/post-a-job` writes to Firestore in parallel. Reconcile weekly by re-running `import-sheet.mjs` with `--dry-run`, which prints the diff.
- `v2/jobs.html` must reproduce the live page's deep links: `?filterD=<institution>` (from the Universities map) has to select the same rows as `?institution=<institution>` does natively. Accept the legacy parameter names as aliases.
- Fix the missing `v2/_PLAN.md` and `v2/_SETUP-FIREBASE.md` — both are referenced by `README.md` and `oa-firebase.js` and neither exists **[verified in repo]**.

### G.4 Cutover

1. Firebase project created, rules published, config pasted, `AUTH_PROVIDERS` matched to the console. Verify a submission end-to-end (`--scan`, then `--dry-run`, then live).
2. Move each `v2/*.html` to its root path, replacing the Awesome Table page: `jobs.html`, `candidates.html`, `placements.html`, `recent-faculty.html`, `previous-markets.html`, `universities.html`. Switch `oa-nav.js` back to the relative hrefs of `navigationMenu.js` (or make `navigationMenu.js` absolute site-wide and delete the duplicate).
3. Add the new pages (`post-a-job`, `submit-candidate`, `alerts`, `feedback`, `about`/what's-new) to **`assets/js/navigationMenu.js`**, **`sitemap.xml`** and optionally `partials/footer.html`. Remove the `noindex` metas.
4. Delete the `<script src="https://awesome-table.com/AwesomeTableInclude.js">` tag from all 17 pages — it is a leaf dependency. **Keep** jQuery, dropotron, skel, util.js and main.js on every page, or mobile navigation disappears below 840 px.
5. Point the Google Forms' confirmation text at the new form, then close them. Keep the sheets read-only as an archive.
6. Post a `changelog.json` entry dated that day — that is what e-mails the "website updates" subscribers.
7. Cancel the Awesome Tables subscription.

**Rollback** at any point: revert the page files (the sheets and the Forms are untouched) and re-add the AT script tag.

## H. Risks and gotchas

**Data / pipeline**
1. **Never count a capped file's rows for a headline number.** /lit/ under-reported by thousands doing exactly that; hence `recent-counts.json`. Trust the tally only when it is ≥ what the rows show, and fall back to counting rows otherwise, so a stale tally can never make the number smaller than the screen.
2. **`JSON.stringify` must be minified with deterministic key order**, or every run diffs and every fire commits + redeploys. Sort object keys explicitly in the counts file.
3. **Write the dataset before stamping Firestore.** The reverse loses a submission on a crash; this order merely re-processes it into a `duplicate`.
4. **A transient API/SMTP failure must leave the doc `pending`**, not rejected — distinguish "not resolvable yet" (retry with a `tries` counter and a max age) from "genuinely invalid".
5. The Action commits generated JSON, so the commit step must be gated `if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/master'` — otherwise a PR branch commits data into its own diff and conflicts with master's refresh commits.
6. `git reset --hard` inside a push-retry drops code commits that landed meanwhile; `--soft` silently reverts them. Use the mixed reset, or the sole-owner `/tmp` replay, or `git pull --rebase`.
7. **Firestore rejects nested arrays and `undefined`.** Adding a field to a client write breaks every create until the rules are republished — ship the one-shot legacy-shape fallback.

**Firebase / privacy**
8. **Anyone can create a `feedback` doc** — no App Check, no anonymous-auth requirement, no per-image byte cap (rules cannot iterate list elements). Decide this up front rather than inheriting it; the mitigations are named in §E.2.
9. The admin inbox does an unpaginated `.get()` of the whole collection **including every base64 screenshot**. Fine at OA's volume; add a limit before it is not.
10. Every account write is best-effort and warn-only, so **an undeployed rule fails silently**. `friendly()`'s `permission-denied` message is the only signal.
11. `registeredUsers` is publicly enumerable by design (§E.2). It must never hold anything but `{t}`.
12. **The repo is public.** A submitter's e-mail in `data/` is a disclosure; a resolution file in `_feedback-resolutions/` must never name the submitter (the mailer looks them up in Firestore by ticket). `oa-checks.yml` enforces the first; the second is a discipline.
13. The Cloud Function's `REGION` must equal the Firestore location or the trigger silently fails to deploy.

**Alerts**
14. **Day-flooring** (`dayStart`/`windowStartFor`) is mandatory wherever item dates are calendar days and marks are timestamps, or same-day items are silently dropped. Keep `--rewind` for the recovery case.
15. With a daily cron, `immediate` and `daily` are behaviourally identical; say so in the UI.
16. `run()` sends one e-mail **per matching alert**, not per recipient — three alerts means three e-mails in one run. Only `--announce` dedupes.
17. **Unsubscribe is not real** in /lit/: the footer links and `List-Unsubscribe` both point at the site, with no token and no `List-Unsubscribe-Post: One-Click`. Bulk senders increasingly require one-click; build a token link now rather than after the first complaint.
18. Editing a shipped resolution file **re-e-mails the submitter** (the content hash changes). Fixing a typo sends a second "resolved" mail.
19. A resolution `url:` is host-validated to https on the site's own hosts; an off-site link makes the whole file a parse error and the ticket is never closed. Update `SITE_HOSTS` to `operationsacademia.org` / `www.operationsacademia.org`.
20. `resolutionSent: true` is stamped for anonymous tickets **without an e-mail being sent** — it means "considered notified", not "delivered".
21. `adminReopen` writes `status:'reopened'`, which the mailer's up-to-date check ignores: a reopened ticket whose resolution file is unchanged is skipped forever. Two close paths coexist (`closedAt` from the page, `resolvedAt`/`resolvedBy:'repo'` from the file) with overlapping-but-different field sets.

**Front end**
22. Inline `onclick="fn('…')"` everywhere means `escAttr` vs `escHtmlAttr` is load-bearing — getting it backwards persists literal backslashes into saved data (`O\'Brien`). Institution names contain apostrophes constantly. **Prefer event delegation with `data-` attributes** and avoid the class entirely.
23. **Card indices are global state** in /lit/ (`paperCardHTML(p, idx)` writes `idx` into element ids and the toggles read `filtered[idx]`), which only works because a second view reassigns `filtered`. Use a `data-id` and look the row up by id.
24. **Accessibility is /lit/'s weak point — do not copy it as-is.** Across 8,260 lines the filter area has two ARIA attributes. `.custom-select` is `div onclick` with no `role="combobox"/"listbox"/"option"`, no `aria-expanded`, no `tabindex`; chips are `span onclick`; card toggles are `span onclick`; there is no live region on the result count. For a public jobs board: buttons for chips and toggles, keyboard-reachable dropdowns (roving tabindex, or native `<select multiple>`/`<details>`), and an `aria-live="polite" role="status"` on the count — which `v2/assets/oa-list.js` already creates **[verified in repo]**.
25. `filterDrop` matches against `item.textContent`, which includes the count — typing a digit filters by count. Surprising when facet values are years.
26. Recompiling `assets/sass/` deletes every site-specific style (§A.1). Add new CSS to `assets/css/main.css` or ship a second `<link>` beside it, as `v2` does.
27. Two copies of the same welcome-state copy already drifted in /lit/ (markup line 969 vs JS line 3408). Keep exactly one source per string.
28. The footer is injected by `fetch`, so it does not appear over `file://` — preview with a local HTTP server (`python3 -m http.server 8899`).
29. `#page-wrapper` is left **unclosed** on `jobs.html`, `candidates.html`, `contact.html`, `survey.html` and `v2/jobs.html` (19 `<div>` vs 18 `</div>`), which puts the footer inside the off-canvas transform on those pages. Close it on every new page.
30. `main.css` `@import`s Google Fonts and Font Awesome at the top of the only stylesheet — blocking, with no local fallback beyond `sans-serif`.
31. The sandbox that produced this research has **no outbound network**, so nothing touching Firestore, SMTP or Drive can be exercised locally; every such pipeline must ship a mock-based offline selftest (the pattern `lit/_scraper/*-selftest.mjs` and `v2/_scraper/selftest.mjs` already follow).

## Open questions

1. **The existing `v2/` prototype was not audited by the research readers.** Only `v2/assets/oa-list.js` was skimmed (582 lines, `mount(cfg)` + declarative filter spec + `passing(skipKey)` + `DERIVE` + `perPage:10`). Everything else in §A.4 is my own direct inspection. Before writing new code, `oa-list.js`, `oa-accounts.js`, `oa-alerts.js`, `oa-feedback.js`, `oa-jobform.js`, `jobs-model.mjs`, `build-jobs.mjs`, `alerts-mailer.mjs`, `_mail.mjs`, `selftest.mjs` and `page-test.mjs` need a real read to determine what is finished, what is stubbed, and how far it already diverges from the /lit/ patterns described in §C.
2. **`v2/_PLAN.md` and `v2/_SETUP-FIREBASE.md` do not exist** although `README.md` and `oa-firebase.js` both point at them. The cutover plan they were meant to hold may exist only in the author's head.
3. **Sheet tab names are only confirmed for the first tab of each file** (`jobsData`, `rawData` ×4, `Universities`). The Drive connector strips sheet-name headings and rejects xlsx export, so every other tab is identified by role + its A1 header. If any tooling addresses tabs by name, verify first.
4. **The `Date posted` / `Deadline` bucket vocabularies are unknown.** Only the branches that currently evaluate are observable (`Older posts`, `Since last June`, `Expired`, `Until filled`, `NA`). The new buckets must be specified from scratch with the owner, not reverse-engineered.
5. **What to do with the 49 never-published job submissions** (raw rows 81‑129, 2025‑08‑13 → 2025‑10‑21) — publish, review, or archive? Several may be expired.
6. **Candidate e-mail addresses**: the old display tab published them; the research does not say whether that was intentional. Confirm before deciding whether `candidates.json` carries a mailto.
7. **Which datasets get their own submission form** — jobs certainly; candidates almost certainly; placements and recent-faculty are curator-maintained today and may stay so (their raw tabs are form-fed but heavily hand-edited afterwards).
8. **Whether the deprecated Universal Analytics snippet is being replaced** (GA4?) — it is dead but ~40 inline handlers depend on the global existing, and the new pages will need an equivalent decision.
9. **The Cloud Function** (instant feedback delivery) — optional. Adding it means a second deploy surface, a hand-maintained renderer copy with no drift guard, and a `REGION` that must match Firestore's location. The 10-minute batch mailer may be enough.
10. **Jekyll and `_`-prefixed paths**: `v2/_scraper/`, `v2/_firestore.rules` and a future `v2/_feedback-resolutions/` are currently unpublished by Pages' default Jekyll build. Confirm that is intended (it is convenient for `_registry.json`) before adding `.nojekyll`.
11. **Alert criteria shape.** `v2/assets/oa-alert-match.js` already fixes `TOPICS = ['jobs','updates','candidates','news']`, but where the "news" items come from — a hand-maintained `news.json`, the changelog, or something else — is not established anywhere in the research or the repo.
12. **Whether `previous-markets` and `universities` are in scope for the first cutover** or can keep their Awesome Table views for a while; the AT script tag would then have to stay on those two pages only.
